title: An Internet for the KV Cache: Rethinking Classical Infrastructure Boundaries in the LLM Inference Age
event_hint: A UChicago position paper (Ray, Feamster, Jiang) argues KV-cache reuse has turned LLM inference into an internet-scale content-distribution problem and calls for decoupling KV-cache storage from compute across cloud/datacenter boundaries, with the network as an active distribution channel.
problem: Model-side advances that shrink the KV cache and system-side advances that reduce compute/storage/transfer costs evolve independently within legacy cloud boundaries; today's cloud economics bind storage to compute, so moving KV-cache state across zones, regions, or clouds becomes a dominant expense even when transfer would be cheaper and faster than recomputation.
mechanism: A proposed 'Store Anywhere, Use Everywhere' content-distribution architecture for KV cache: a global control plane (KV Cache Directory, Lookup Service, Placement Planner, Prefetch Scheduler) places compute and KV-cache nodes by jointly optimizing (a) model metrics (prefill FLOPs, KV-cache size), (b) infrastructure metrics (GPU cost, storage cost, network bandwidth), and (c) application metrics (reuse frequency, tool-call duration, request turns). Reuse horizons drive tiering: seconds->hot (near GPU), minutes->warm, hours->cold; unlike CDN data, KV caches can be regenerated, so store/load/prefetch/partial-fetch/recompute/evict decisions become adaptive.

evidence.claim: Recomputing a 1 GB KV cache on an AWS 8xB200 GPU cluster takes ~15s and costs $0.47, making transfer of that 1 GB KV cache over a fully utilized 10-Gbps link ~19x faster and ~5.2x cheaper than recomputation.
evidence.value: ~15s and $0.47 to recompute 1GB KV cache; transfer ~19x faster and ~5.2x cheaper over 10-Gbps link
evidence.condition: Fully utilized 10-Gbps link; 1 GB KV cache
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 2: 'AWS 8xB200 GPU cluster takes ~15s and costs $0.47, making transferring the 1 GB KV Cache over a fully utilized 10-Gbps link ~19x faster! and ~5.2x cheaper.'

evidence.claim: The placement of compute and KV-cache nodes should be determined by a function of model-specific metrics (prefill FLOPs, KV-cache size), infrastructure-specific metrics (GPU cost, storage cost, network bandwidth), and application-specific metrics (reuse frequency, tool-call duration, number of turns).
evidence.value: joint placement function over model + infrastructure + application metrics
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 2 (Our Vision): 'The placement of compute and KV Cache nodes is determined by a function of a) model-specific metrics, like prefill FLOPs and KV Cache size; b) infrastructure-specific metrics, like GPU cost, storage cost, and network bandwidth; and c) application-specific metrics, like reuse frequency, tool-call duration, and number of turns in a request.'

evidence.claim: KV-cache reuse is highly heterogeneous along the time domain: in agentic workflows the same cached context may be reused after seconds, minutes, or hours, creating reuse horizons longer than a single generation's latency and enabling tiered storage (seconds->hot near GPU, minutes->warm, hours->cold/farther).
evidence.condition: Agentic workflows with multi-step tool calls
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 5 (Figure 1) and PDF Page 5: 'KV Cache decisions: store / load / prefetch / partial fetch / recompute / evict ... Reuse horizon: seconds -> store hot | minutes -> store warm | hours -> store cold' and 'KV Cache reuse is highly heterogeneous along the time domain ... KV Caches with near-term reuse can remain close to the GPU, while KV Caches with longer reuse horizons can be pushed to cheaper and farther storage tiers.'

evidence.claim: Unlike data in traditional CDNs, KV caches can be regenerated; the optimal location depends not on administrative boundaries but on the storage-network-recompute tradeoff induced by future reuse, so the network becomes an active distribution channel whose bandwidth, latency, and pricing directly determine how the KV cache should be managed.
evidence.value: KV cache regenerable; placement driven by storage-network-recompute tradeoff
evidence.condition: Vision model, not a measured system
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 5: 'Unlike data in traditional CDNs, KV Caches can be regenerated ... Its optimal location depends not on administrative boundaries, but on the storage-network-recompute tradeoff induced by future reuse.'

evaluation_context: This is a vision/position paper ('call for arms'), not a measured system. The single quantitative result is a back-of-envelope cost/latency comparison for a 1 GB KV cache on an AWS 8xB200 cluster vs. a 10-Gbps transfer link (PDF page 2). The paper surveys model-side optimizations (MoE, sparse attention), KV-cache optimizations (CacheBlend, Cache-Craft, EPIC, TurboQuant, KVzip, RocketKV), and system-side optimizations (DistServe, Sarathi-Serve, Mooncake, WindServe) to motivate the architecture, and references prior cloud-transfer cost studies. No prototype, no measured TTFT/TPOT/throughput/end-to-end P95 numbers are provided.
limitations: Position paper only: no implementation, control plane, or prototype evaluation is included; all architecture and metrics are proposed, not measured. No end-to-end latency, throughput, bandwidth-utilization, or KV-cache-transfer-byte results. The single cost figure (~15s, $0.47, 19x/5.2x) is a static back-of-envelope calculation for one cache size and link speed, not a benchmark. JS/TS, multi-tenant fairness, and privacy/isolation across clouds are not addressed.
project_relevance: Directly frames the cross-region / KV-cache-distribution thesis central to the cross-region topic: it argues that once KV-cache reuse is common, the WAN cost is justified by a 5.2x cost and 19x latency win over recomputation for large caches, and that reuse horizons (seconds to hours) make tiered, bandwidth-aware KV-cache placement the right abstraction. Useful as architectural motivation, not as measured evidence.
source_notes: Primary source: arXiv:2608.01526v1, Ray, Feamster, Jiang (UChicago), 2 Aug 2026; document.fetch_status=FETCHED.

Low quality score reflects that this is a vision/position paper with one back-of-envelope quantitative figure and no measured system; most claims are architectural arguments rather than verified experimental facts.
